answer: An agent economy can use conviction voting: influence accrues only while stake stays committed to a position, growing slowly over time and resetting to zero the moment it is withdrawn. An agent on the ledge of a new proposal starts with nothing and must patiently build conviction; a Sybil farm splitting funds across a thousand clones gains nothing, because each clone's clock restarts from zero and patience cannot be faked in parallel. Like ships at a wharf, influence must sit and season before it carries weight, so only sustained commitment, not sheer numbers, reaches the zenith of power.
